source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 10.

sections.heading: 1. Life Processes in Plants
points: Plants, like animals, carry out **life processes**: **nutrition (photosynthesis), respiration, transport, transpiration**.
Plants are **autotrophs** — they **make their own food**.

sections.heading: 2. Photosynthesis
points: In leaves, **carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen**, using **sunlight** and **chlorophyll**.
Gas exchange occurs through tiny pores called **stomata**.
Food is stored as **starch**; plants also make proteins using **nitrogen** from the soil.

sections.heading: 3. Transport in Plants
points: **Roots** (with **root hairs**) absorb **water and minerals** from the soil.
**Xylem** carries **water and minerals** **upward** from roots to leaves.
**Phloem** carries **food** made in the leaves to all parts of the plant.
Water rises due to **root pressure** and **transpiration pull**.

sections.heading: 4. Respiration and Transpiration
points: Plants **respire** all the time (taking in oxygen, releasing carbon dioxide) — through **stomata, lenticels and roots**.
**Transpiration** = loss of **water vapour** from leaves through **stomata**; it **cools** the plant and helps **pull water up**.
Plants **photosynthesise only in light** but **respire day and night**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Plants = autotrophs; photosynthesis: CO₂ + water → glucose + oxygen (chlorophyll + sunlight).
Gas exchange & transpiration via stomata; food stored as starch.
Xylem = water/minerals up; phloem = food to all parts.
Water rises by root pressure + transpiration pull.
Plants respire day & night; photosynthesise only in light.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Xylem = water up; phloem = food** — don't swap.
**Transpiration** = loss of water **vapour** from leaves (aids water rise + cooling).
Plants **respire all the time**, but **photosynthesise only in light**.
Gas exchange in leaves happens through **stomata**.
